title: Dispatch Guidance — Ordering a Stop on Refined Fuels and Propane Accounts
content:
How a stop is ordered on an account under Refined Fuels and Propane Accounts decides when it happens and what it costs.

**Automatic schedule.** On a keep-full programme the truck comes when the degree-day model or a gauge reading puts the tank at or below the programme's trigger percentage, and it fills to the programme's fill-to percentage rather than to the top, because room must be left for expansion.

**Called-in stops.** On a will-call programme nothing happens until the member calls, and the call needs the programme's notice in business days before the route is run. A member who calls on the day of the route is fitted in where the load allows and charged nothing extra, and one who cannot wait is delivered as an emergency at the emergency fee.

**Under-minimum loads.** A delivery under the programme's minimum gallons carries the minimum delivery fee, which is charged on the stop rather than per gallon.

**Run-outs.** A tank that has run completely out is not refilled until a leak check has been done where the programme requires one, and the check is a service call in its own right.

**Seasonal hold.** Deliveries are suspended while the account stands on seasonal hold, and a member on hold who calls for fuel is brought back into service first. Seasonal hold runs no longer than the programme's hold maximum in calendar days from the day it was set, after which the account returns to service on its own.

## Condition and result, set out as a table

| The tank or the account stands thus | What follows |
| --- | --- |
| On an automatic schedule, gauge at or below the programme's trigger | A stop is scheduled, and the tank is filled to the programme's fill-to reading |
| On a called-in programme, notice given at the programme's business days or more | The stop is fitted to the route |
| On a called-in programme, called on the day the route is run | Fitted in where the load allows, at no extra charge |
| On a called-in programme, called at short notice and unable to wait | Delivered as an emergency, at the emergency fee |
| Gallons pumped fall under the programme's minimum | The minimum delivery fee is charged on the stop |
| The tank has run completely out, on a programme requiring the check | Not refilled until a leak check has been done |
| The account stands on seasonal hold | Deliveries are suspended; a member who calls for fuel is brought back into service first |
| Seasonal hold has run the programme's maximum in calendar days from the day it was set | The account returns to service on its own |

## Boundary illustration (hypothetical)

A gauge reads exactly the programme's trigger percentage. The rule reads "at or below", so the reading on the boundary schedules the stop. A gauge one point above the trigger does not.
